challenges.name: domain-errors-http-quiz
challenges.title: Read the error path: which filter answered, and what the mobile app does next
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the enrollments API: a 500 that slipped past the domain error filter, and the mobile app's retry policy meeting the new 409 response.

questions.explanation: True. @Catch(DomainError) tells Nest to call this filter only for exceptions that are instances of DomainError (or its subclasses). A TypeError is not, so Nest falls back to its built-in global exception filter, which answers every exception that is not an HttpException with exactly this body: {"statusCode":500,"message":"Internal server error"}. The Content-Type confirms it: the custom filter would have written application/problem+json. To give unknown errors the same problem format and a correlation id, use @Catch() with no argument and handle the unknown case yourself, still without putting the error's message in the body. The misconception is that a global filter sees every error; it sees the types listed in @Catch.

questions.question:
The mobile app's API client:

// mobile/api/client.ts
// retry a request when it fails with a network error or status >= 500:
// up to 3 retries, after 1 s, 2 s and 4 s. Never retry a 4xx.

Access log before the fix (one tap on Enroll, the learner was already enrolled):
10:41:02.118 POST /enrollments 500 31ms
10:41:03.164 POST /enrollments 500 28ms
10:41:05.201 POST /enrollments 500 30ms
10:41:09.236 POST /enrollments 500 29ms

After the fix, the API answers the same request with:
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{"type":"https://api.codedev.test/problems/already-enrolled","title":"Already enrolled","status":409, ...}

Statement: "The app will still send this POST four times per tap until its retry policy is changed as well."
questions.explanation: False. The retries came from the status code, not from the app: a 500 says "the server failed, trying again might work", and the client's policy retries exactly that. With the domain error mapped to 409, the response falls in the 4xx range the policy never retries, so one tap now produces one request and the app can show "You are already enrolled" from the problem body. Choosing the right status is how the server tells every client, including ones you do not control, whether a retry can help. The misconception is that each client needs its own fix; a correct status code fixes all of them at once.

challenges.name: map-domain-errors-to-problems
challenges.title: Map domain errors to problem responses
challenges.description: Every domain error from the CodeDev enrollment service came back as 500 "Internal server error", so the mobile app retried enrollments that had already failed with a conflict. The service throws typed domain errors and knows nothing about HTTP; write the one function at the edge that turns anything thrown into a response: toProblemResponse(error: unknown, req: { method, path, headers }, newId: () => string) returns { status, headers, body }. Correlation id: use req.headers["x-correlation-id"] when it matches /^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,64}$/; otherwise call newId() exactly once and use its value (never call it when the header is usable). Headers: { "Content-Type": "application/problem+json", "X-Correlation-Id": id }. Body: { type: "https://api.codedev.test/problems/" + slug, title, status, detail, instance: req.path, correlationId: id } plus extensions. Match with instanceof: CourseNotFound -> 404, slug course-not-found, title "Course not found", detail "Course <courseId> does not exist."; AlreadyEnrolled -> 409, already-enrolled, "Already enrolled", "You are already enrolled in <courseId>."; PrerequisitesMissing -> 422, prerequisites-missing, "Prerequisites missing", "Finish <missing joined by ", "> before enrolling in <courseId>.", extension missing (the list); ValidationFailed -> 400, validation-failed, "Invalid request", "<number of errors> field(s) failed validation.", extension errors: [{ field, message }] (copy only those two keys - the errors may carry the rejected value); NotAllowed -> 403, not-allowed, "Not allowed", "You are not allowed to <action>."; PaymentRequired -> 402, payment-required, "Payment required", "<courseId> requires a premium plan.", extension priceVnd. Anything else - a plain Error or TypeError, a thrown string or null, an object that only looks like a domain error, or a DomainError subclass not in this list - is 500, slug internal-error, title "Internal server error", detail "An unexpected error occurred. Quote the correlation id when you contact support.", and never contains the error's message. Input (stdin): { "cases": [{ "error": { "kind", ... }, "method"?, "path"?, "correlationId"? }] } (correlationId is sent as the x-correlation-id header; newId() returns gen-0001, gen-0002, ... per test) prints each response with JSON keys sorted; { "generate": { "count", "seed" } } prints the responses per status, the number of newId() calls and how many responses contained internal text.
hints: Two questions decide every response: which status tells the client whether trying again can help, and which parts of the error is the client allowed to read? What should happen to an error you cannot name?

Look at instanceof for each class in the table (an object with name "CourseNotFound" is not a CourseNotFound), at the order of your checks if you ever add a check for the DomainError base class, and at what you copy from ValidationFailed.errors. Decide the correlation id once, at the top, before you know which branch you will take.

A similar mapping for a submissions API: SubmissionTooLarge(limitKb: 64) -> 413 with detail "The submission is larger than 64 KB." and extension limitKb 64; LanguageNotSupported("cobol") -> 422; new Error("ENOSPC: no space left on device, write '/var/runner/tmp/abc'") -> 500 with the fixed text "An unexpected error occurred." and no path; header x-correlation-id "ok-12345678" is kept, "ok 1" is replaced by the next generated id.
